debarment_guidelines.md.authority: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, Government of India (Procurement Policy Division)

sections.Exclusion of debarred firms from partici: Debarred bidders are not eligible to participate in procurement processes for the debarment period.
sections.Scope of the DoE guidelines — OM No. F.1: Issuing facts of the DoE debarment guidelines OM.
sections.Statutory basis — GFR 2017, Rule 151 (De: Statutory grounds and periods for debarment reproduced in the OM: conviction cases (up to 3 years), Code of Integrity breach (up to 2 years), right of representation.
sections.Two types of debarment — as cited in off: Debarment by the bidder's own Ministry/Department, or universal debarment across all Ministries/Departments when ordered by the Department of Expenditure.
sections.Version note: No later amendment verified from an official source; where applicability of a later amendment is in question, version applicability requires review.

gfr_2017_procurement.md.authority: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

sections.Rule 142 — Scope of procurement chapter: Defines the scope of the GFR procurement chapter for all Ministries/Departments.
sections.Rule 144 — Fundamental principles of pub: Sets the binding yardsticks for all public procurement: fair and transparent procedure, documented decisions, reasonable pricing, and equitable treatment of suppliers.
sections.Rule 150 — Registration of suppliers: Requires verification of supplier credentials, past performance and financial background before registration; suppliers making false declarations can be removed.
sections.Rule 151 — Debarment from bidding: Statutory grounds and periods for debarring bidders: up to 3 years for conviction cases, up to 2 years for breach of the Code of Integrity, with a right of representation.
sections.Rule 153 — Reserved items and purchase/p: Legal basis for mandatory procurement and purchase/price preference policies, including preference on grounds of promoting locally manufactured goods (the basis of the Make in India Order).
sections.Rule 155 — Purchase committee certificat: Requires the purchase committee to certify the recommended supplier is not debarred.
sections.Rule 157 — Demand not to be split: Prohibits splitting demands to avoid sanction thresholds or procurement procedures.
sections.Rule 158 — Purchase of goods by obtainin: Standard bid methods: Advertised Tender Enquiry, Limited Tender Enquiry, Two-Stage Bidding.
sections.Rule 173 — Transparency, competition, fa: Requires transparent bidding documents, eligibility criteria, public bid opening, and disclosure of rejection reasons.
sections.Rule 175 — Code of Integrity: Prohibits bribery, misrepresentation, collusion, and false declarations in tender participation; breach can lead to debarment.

mii_order_2017.md.authority: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India (Public Procurement Section)

sections.Para 1 — Legal basis: The Order is issued pursuant to Rule 153(iii) of the General Financial Rules 2017.
sections.Para 10(b) — Eligibility conditions must: Eligibility conditions on turnover, production capability and financial strength must not unreasonably exclude local suppliers.
sections.Para 14 — Powers to grant exemption and: The administrative department, with Minister's written approval, may reduce local content or the preference margin, or exempt items, for a particular procurement.
sections.Para 2 — Definitions: Defines local content, Class-I/Class-II local supplier, Non-local supplier, L1, and margin of purchase preference.
sections.Para 20 — Transitional provision: The Order does not apply to tenders issued before the Order.
sections.Para 2A — Special treatment for items co: PLI-scheme manufacturers are treated as deemed Class-II local suppliers for the notified period.
sections.Para 3 — Eligibility of suppliers for di: Only Class-I suppliers may bid where the nodal ministry notifies sufficient local capacity; Class-I and Class-II may bid otherwise; non-local suppliers only in global tender enquiries.
sections.Para 3.1 — Mandatory sourcing from Class: Items notified with sufficient local capacity must be sourced from Class-I local suppliers in SI/EPC/turnkey/service tenders.
sections.Para 3A — Purchase preference mechanism: How purchase preference is given to Class-I local suppliers (divisible and non-divisible procurement); Class-II suppliers get no purchase preference.
sections.Para 3B(e) — Tender-specific award crite: Procuring entities may stipulate their own tender-specific award criteria within the Order's broad policy guidelines.
sections.Para 4 — Exemption of small purchases: Procurements below Rs. 5 lakh are exempt; splitting to avoid the Order is prohibited.
sections.Para 5 — Minimum local content: Default minimum local content: 50% for Class-I, 20% for Class-II; nodal ministries may prescribe only a higher percentage for specific items.
sections.Para 6 — Margin of purchase preference: The margin of purchase preference is 20%.
sections.Para 7 — Requirement for specification i: Minimum local content, margin of purchase preference and procedure must be specified in the tender notice and not varied during the procurement.
sections.Para 9 — Verification of local content: Self-certification of local content at tendering; auditor/CA certification for procurements above Rs. 10 crore; false declarations breach the Code of Integrity and can lead to debarment up to 2 years.

udyam_msme.md.authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India

sections.Classification criteria — S.O. 2119(E) d: Micro/small/medium classification thresholds on investment in plant & machinery/equipment and turnover.
sections.Composite criteria of classification: Classification uses a composite of investment and turnover criteria.
sections.Exports exclusion from turnover: Export turnover is not counted in the turnover limits for any MSME category.
sections.Protection of non-tax benefits on upward: Enterprises reclassified upwards keep non-tax benefits of the earlier category for 3 years.
sections.Udyam Registration — process: Online, free, paperless, self-declaration based registration; Aadhaar and PAN required; investment/turnover auto-fetched from PAN/GSTIN-linked government databases.
sections.Version applicability note: S.O. 2119(E) thresholds apply before 01.04.2025; S.O. 1364(E) thresholds apply on/after 01.04.2025; where the evaluation date is unknown, version applicability requires review.
